Panel QTT (Callaway-Li 2019)

Source: R/panel_qtt.R
panel_qtt.Rd

Computes Quantile Treatment Effects on the Treated (QTT) and the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) using the three-period panel identification strategy of Callaway and Li (2019). Handles two-period (one post + two pre-treatment periods) and staggered treatment adoption via ptetools. Requires panel data for both groups.

Identification. Under a copula stability assumption and distributional parallel trends on changes, the counterfactual distribution \(F_{Y(0)^{\text{post}}|D=1}\) is recovered from three periods of panel data without requiring rank invariance.

pre_copula. Controls which pre-treatment periods are used as the copula-transfer base for post-treatment cells (g, g+e):

"long" (default)

pre2 is as many periods before pre1 as the post period is after it, matching the copula window to the event horizon. pre1 is the last period at least anticipation before g (in units of the time variable). Cells where pre2 does not exist in the data are excluded from aggregation with two-step weight renormalization.

"short"

pre2 is the period just before pre1, always anchored at treatment onset.

Pre-test placebo cells always use the sliding base regardless of pre_copula.

Usage

panel_qtt(
  yname,
  gname,
  tname,
  idname,
  data,
  xformula = ~1,
  cond_dist = c("qr", "dr"),
  weightsname = NULL,
  clustervars = NULL,
  control_group = "notyettreated",
  anticipation = 0,
  alp = 0.05,
  cband = TRUE,
  biters = 100,
  cl = 1,
  gt_type = "att",
  probs = NULL,
  pre_copula = "long"
)

Arguments

yname

Name of the outcome variable.

gname

Name of the treatment group variable (first treatment period; 0 for never-treated units).

tname

Name of the time period variable.

idname

Name of the unit id variable (required).

data

A data frame.

xformula

One-sided formula for covariates. Default ~1. Each unit's covariates are taken from the earliest period the group-time cell uses (the second pre-treatment period), so they are fixed across all three periods.

cond_dist

How conditional distributions are estimated when xformula has covariates: "qr" (default) for quantile regression or "dr" for distribution regression. See cic_gt. Ignored without covariates.

weightsname

Name of the sampling weights column. Default NULL.

clustervars

Name of a column in data to cluster standard errors on, in addition to idname (as in did::att_gt()): one variable, constant over time within each unit. Default NULL clusters at the unit level. With the empirical bootstrap, whole clusters are resampled.

control_group

"notyettreated" (default) or "nevertreated".

anticipation

Anticipation, in units of the time variable. Default 0.

alp

Significance level. Default 0.05.

cband

Logical; uniform confidence band if TRUE (default).

biters

Number of bootstrap iterations. Default 100.

cl

Number of parallel clusters. Default 1.

gt_type

"att" (default) or "qtt".

probs

Quantile grid for gt_type = "qtt". Default seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05).

pre_copula

"long" (default) or "short". See Details.

Value

For gt_type = "att", a pte_emp_boot object. For gt_type = "qtt", a pte_qtt object.

Discrete outcomes

Quantile treatment effects usually require a continuous outcome. With mass points (e.g. many zeros) or few distinct values, quantiles jump and effects at quantiles inside a mass point are 0 by construction; identification based on ranks or quantile functions (change-in-changes, quantile DiD, the panel and distributional DiD copula arguments) only bounds the effects (Athey and Imbens 2006, Section 4); and bootstrap inference for quantiles can be unreliable. The estimators warn (once per call, class qte_discrete_outcome) when more than 10\ outcome's observations share one value or it takes at most 20 distinct values, across all groups and periods; the thresholds are the options qte.mass_point_tol and qte.discrete_n_unique. The diagnostics are returned as outcome_discreteness. cdf_did is identified for discrete outcomes.

Repeated cross sections

cic(), qdid(), mdid(), cdf_did() and lou_qtt(lagged_outcome_cov = FALSE) also work with repeated cross sections (panel = FALSE; idname not needed). Without covariates they use only each period's outcome distributions, so on panel data the estimates are the same either way; the standard errors differ, because the bootstrap then resamples observations rather than units. Some things need the same units in several periods and so require panel data: ddid() (each comparison unit's change over time), panel_qtt() (the copula between periods), the lagged outcome in lou_qtt(), and gt_type = "qott" (the distribution of individual treatment effects).

References

Callaway, Brantly and Tong Li. “Quantile Treatment Effects in Difference-in-Differences Models with Panel Data.” Quantitative Economics 10(4), pp. 1579-1618, 2019.

See also

cic, qdid, mdid, ddid

Examples

# \donttest{
data(mpdta, package = "did")

## Panel QTT with rolling pre-period copula (default pre_copula = "long")
res <- panel_qtt(yname = "lemp", gname = "first.treat", tname = "year",
                 idname = "countyreal", data = mpdta,
                 gt_type = "qtt", probs = seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1), biters = 20)
summary(res)
